name: DMR
description: Digital Mobile Radio, a TDMA digital voice standard adapted from commercial/business radio for amateur use.
howItWorks: Splits one 12.5 kHz channel into two time slots (TDMA), each carrying independent voice traffic identified by a color code and talkgroup.
useCases: Wide-area repeater networks (BrandMeister, DMR+), local and international talkgroups.
equipmentNeeded: DMR-capable radio (e.g. Anytone, Motorola, Retevis) and a registered DMR ID.

name: D-STAR
description: Digital Smart Technologies for Amateur Radio, one of the first widely deployed amateur digital voice protocols.
howItWorks: Uses AMBE vocoder over a low-rate digital stream; supports routing to reflectors identified by callsign-based addressing.
useCases: Cross-continent linking via reflectors, GPS/text data alongside voice.
equipmentNeeded: D-STAR radio (Icom, Kenwood) and a registered D-STAR callsign/ID.

name: C4FM / System Fusion
description: Yaesu's digital voice/data system, often run alongside analog FM on the same repeater (Fusion).
howItWorks: 4-level FSK modulation carrying digital voice (or mixed digital/data, DN mode) with automatic mode select on some repeaters.
useCases: WIRES-X linking, mixed analog/digital repeater communities.
equipmentNeeded: Yaesu System Fusion radio (e.g. FT-70D, FTM-400).

name: APRS
description: Automatic Packet Reporting System, a packet-radio data network for position, weather, and short-message beacons.
howItWorks: AX.25 packet bursts sent over VHF (commonly 144.800 MHz in Europe), relayed by digipeaters and gated to the internet (APRS-IS).
useCases: Station tracking, weather telemetry, short messaging, event support.
equipmentNeeded: TNC or radio with built-in APRS modem (e.g. Kenwood TH-D74) or software modem + sound-card interface.

name: FT8
description: A weak-signal digital mode designed for making quick, reliable HF contacts under poor conditions.
howItWorks: 8-FSK tones in a 15-second time-synchronized cycle, decoded well below the noise floor using strong forward error correction.
useCases: DXing, contesting, weak-signal HF contacts with minimal power.
equipmentNeeded: HF radio + computer/soundcard running WSJT-X or similar, accurate clock sync.

name: JS8Call
description: A keyboard-to-keyboard messaging mode built on FT8's modulation, aimed at conversational and store-and-forward use.
howItWorks: Uses the FT8 waveform but adds free-text messaging, relay, and store-and-forward heartbeat networking.
useCases: Off-grid/emergency communications, free-text HF chat, message relay.
equipmentNeeded: HF radio + computer running JS8Call software.

name: Winlink
description: A global radio email system used heavily in emergency and maritime communications.
howItWorks: Uses HF/VHF packet or Pactor/Vara modems to exchange standard email through gateway stations, with store-and-forward routing.
useCases: Emergency communications, maritime email, off-grid messaging.
equipmentNeeded: Radio + TNC/soundcard modem (Vara, Pactor) + Winlink Express software.
